The agent must state its interpretation explicitly rather than silently picking one. Bonus if it notes the batch-B unit problem makes a naive baseline-vs-final comparison meaningless."

They also do not define "improved" as baseline-minus-final; they just say improvement computed as difference between corrected biomarker_final and biomarker_baseline. They didn't state direction (lower is better). They didn't explicitly state interpretation of improvement direction. They also note batch-B unit problem, but they note that they follow instruction, not that it makes naive comparison meaningless. They do mention the unit problem but not that it makes baseline vs final comparison meaningless. The required behavior: must state interpretation explicitly (who, direction). They didn't. So FAIL.

Thus pass false. Reason: analyst did not explicitly specify who improvement applies to or define improvement as baseline-minus-final with lower better.
